h1: The booking that stores someone else's appointment in a language they didn't choose to disclose

criteria.h1: The booking that stores someone else's appointment in a language they didn't choose to disclose
tableRows: Easy AppointmentsDocumented self-hosted appointment plugin marketed for service businesses (plugin version 4.0.3). WordPress admin screens cover locations, services, workers, an appointments list, a customer list, custom form fields, and CSV export. An assignment booking is a booking you create; a service name such as ASL medical, Dari legal, or Spanish IEP meeting is a label you configure. Neither is a documented default. Language-pair, appointment-type, setting, client-name, or special-instructions questions are custom fields you add (textarea, select, input, or checkbox); they are not documented defaults. A booking is a schedule, not a confidentiality agreement — and a CSV export of assignment visits next to a client name and a language pair is still a proxy-subject row after an institution booked for someone who never saw the form. Emails can include those custom fields and copy the appointment off-site. An optional GDPR setting can auto-remove customer data older than six months; that is not a default purge. Google Calendar, SMS, and payments are Pro. Google reCAPTCHA is optional. Public booking-form browser hosts are unverified. | Interpreter assignment bookings stored on your WordPress site | Browser hosts not verified | Not assessed | Not tested | None | WordPress.org listingv4.0.3 readme.txt (SVN)

Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form BuilderDocumented self-hosted form builder (plugin version 1.58.1). The listing states Forminator stores and organizes submissions so you can sort, analyze, and manage responses, and includes a free file-upload field with multi-file support. Version 1.58.1 helper-fields.php forminator_upload_root() writes under the WordPress uploads directory plus /forminator/, with per-form hashed subfolders from forminator_get_upload_path(). upload.php stores files through that path. Language-pair, appointment-type, setting, client-name, or special-instructions questions are fields you add; they are not documented defaults. Completing the form can store a client name next to a language pair, an appointment type, a medical or legal or school setting, special instructions, and optional case-document or meeting-agenda uploads — typed once by an institution for someone who never saw the form into the same tables as a newsletter signup. A booking request is not a confidentiality agreement. An appointment-type field is the booker's description, not the subject's disclosure. A client-name field is a third person who never saw the form. An uploaded agenda is the institution's document in uploads/forminator, not the subject's consent — and a staff login can open "ASL, oncology follow-up" next to a name the patient never typed. Notification emails can copy field values and files off-site. Optional Stripe, PayPal, HubSpot, Mailchimp, and webhook integrations send data only when you enable them. Public form-page browser hosts are unverified. | Proxy-subject intake entries stored in WordPress; optional case-document and meeting-agenda uploads in the site uploads/forminator folder | Browser hosts not verified | Not assessed | Not tested | None | WordPress.org listingv1.58.1 readme.txt (SVN)v1.58.1 helper-fields.php (upload root)v1.58.1 upload.php
